title: Browser runtime and dependencies
requirement: Load one HTML document containing the UI, styles, application state and inline JavaScript; obtain Three.js r128, Tailwind CSS and Google Fonts from external CDNs.
verification_or_acceptance: Inspect script/link dependencies and WebGLRenderer construction.
limitation: No application backend, database, package lock, bundled offline assets or explicitly required WebGL2 context is implemented. The Three.js renderer requires a working WebGL context.

title: Model and route graph
requirement: Represent the venue as 26 hardcoded XYZ nodes and 32 bidirectional edges, including direction-specific instructions, slope, stairs, elevator, shade, surface and modeled noise attributes. Build 64 directed adjacency entries.
verification_or_acceptance: Executed graph reports 26 nodes and 32 undirected edges.
limitation: Coordinates and labels are demo data, not surveyed venue facts. Surface labels are stored but do not constrain routing; widths, closures, crowds, elevator outages and waiting-time feeds are absent.

title: Preset selection and initial route
requirement: Offer three start presets and five destinations; initialize Gate 29 drop-off to Section 308, with step-free enabled, standard 1.4 m/s speed, wheelchair eye height, and playback paused.
verification_or_acceptance: All 15 preset pairs yield a route under all eight combinations of the three routing switches.
limitation: No free-address search, GPS-selected start or arbitrary ticket/seat lookup is implemented.

title: Weighted shortest-path routing
requirement: Run Dijkstra over the modeled graph. Set base length to max(4 m, rounded 3D Euclidean distance to 0.1 m); add 10 cost units for an elevator edge, add 1.8 times length for noise >=74 dB when low-sensory is selected, add 1.6 times length for an unshaded edge when shade is selected, then multiply stair-edge cost by 0.85 in standard mode.
verification_or_acceptance: 120 preset/option configurations executed; shade changes 14 of 60 paired comparisons.
limitation: The objective is a weighted preference cost, not guaranteed shortest physical distance or minimum travel time. The 10-unit lift penalty is not included in displayed ETA.

title: Step-free exclusion
requirement: When stepFreeOnly is true, exclude each edge with hasStairs=true or maxSlopePct>8.33 before considering its cost. Standard mode permits these edges.
verification_or_acceptance: All 60 step-free configurations executed across 15 pairs and four preference combinations have zero stair edges and no traversed slope metadata above 8.33%.
limitation: This is a graph metadata rule, not an ADA compliance certificate. Width, landings, cross-slope, condition and actual elevator operation are not validated.

title: Route metrics
requirement: Show route meters and converted feet, rounded ETA of at least one minute, maximum modeled slope, number of stair edges, length-weighted shaded percentage, arithmetic length-weighted noise metadata, and runs of consecutive elevator edges.
verification_or_acceptance: Default step-free route: 92.3 m, 5.8% maximum modeled grade, 0 stair edges, 1 elevator run, 83% shade, modeled average 66 dB.
limitation: A stair-edge count is not the number of stair treads. Noise is not a physical/logarithmic sound-exposure calculation. Elevator waiting and boarding time are absent from ETA.

title: Recalculation and missing routes
requirement: Recompute when start, destination, route switches or speed change. Reset progress for a changed endpoint; preserve and clamp traveled meters for preference/speed changes. If route calculation returns null, show a no-compliant-route toast.
verification_or_acceptance: Trace each selector/checkbox handler to recalculateRoute and inspect its null branch.
limitation: The null branch does not clear a previous route. Endpoint state and old rendered route can therefore disagree if a future graph change makes a selection unreachable.

title: Procedural 3D scene
requirement: Render a procedural Coliseum-style scene and route overlays in separate Three.js groups, with a 64-degree perspective camera, alpha-enabled WebGL rendering, and device pixel ratio capped at 2.
verification_or_acceptance: Inspect renderer, camera, scene-group construction and procedural environment builder.
limitation: Geometry is constructed by the code; it is not a georeferenced scan or calibrated digital twin. No measured frame-rate guarantee is enforced.

title: Route guidance graphics
requirement: Rebuild floor/ramp ribbons, floating 3D chevrons, elevator columns, junction rings and destination beacons from the route. Use green for default step-free guidance, amber for standard guidance, and yellow/black in high-contrast mode.
verification_or_acceptance: Inspect rebuild3DARWayfinding; chevrons use about 4.5 m spacing normally and 2.4 m on elevator edges.
limitation: These are simulation-space graphics. World anchoring to a real venue is not implemented; scene object existence alone does not verify visibility or alignment.

title: HUD and direction cues
requirement: Update the instruction banner, meters/feet to the next waypoint, floor/compass, relative clock-face cue, modeled noise label, elevator transition banner and arrival message from route progress and camera yaw.
verification_or_acceptance: Inspect updateNavHud; off-screen cue appears when heading differs by more than 0.95 radians and arrival is more than 1 m away.
limitation: The displayed values are derived from simulation state, not real-time location, acoustic measurements or venue operational status.

title: Mini-map and beacon projection
requirement: Draw an expandable 2D mini-map with the route, user pose and destination. Project selected route-waypoint labels into screen space; hide labels outside view limits or nearer than 3.5 m or farther than 145 m.
verification_or_acceptance: Inspect drawMiniMap and updateProjectedBeacons plus expand/collapse handler.
limitation: Label clipping reduces overlap but does not measure viewport obstruction or guarantee an uncluttered display on every device.

title: Playback and progress controls
requirement: Provide play/pause/replay, speeds of 0.9, 1.4 and 3.2 m/s, a 0–1000 route scrubber, previous/next waypoint buttons and clickable waypoint entries. Interpolate position along route edges; stop auto-walk at arrival.
verification_or_acceptance: Trace progress changes to sampleRouteAtDistance and the arrival clamp.
limitation: This moves a virtual user; it does not detect walking. Frame time is capped at 0.05 s, so speed is not guaranteed to match wall-clock time under severe rendering stalls.

title: View and keyboard controls
requirement: Use pointer dragging to change yaw/pitch, WASD for planar free movement, arrow keys for movement/turning, Space for playback, R for recentering, and Escape for closing panels. Do not apply keyboard shortcuts while an input/select/textarea has focus.
verification_or_acceptance: Trace pointer and key handlers; manual movement is 5.5 model meters per simulated second.
limitation: Manual free movement has no collision detection or route snapping and does not advance route progress. Guidance can remain tied to an older route segment. Buttons are not excluded from the global Space shortcut.

title: Eye-height adjustment
requirement: Toggle target eye height between 1.20 m and 1.65 m above the current modeled position; interpolate normally and snap to target when reduced motion is active.
verification_or_acceptance: Inspect toggle assignment and currentEyeHeight interpolation.
limitation: These are preset simulated offsets, not automatic calibration to an individual or a physical camera.

title: Camera-overlay mode
requirement: On request, obtain video with rear-facing camera preferred and audio disabled. On success, hide the stadium, show video behind transparent route overlays, and retain virtual navigation state. On exit, stop stream tracks and restore the simulated scene.
status: Static source evidence; device path untested
verification_or_acceptance: Inspect getUserMedia options, success/failure branches and track stop logic; actual device permission/camera testing remains outstanding.
limitation: Requires a browser context supporting camera permission, typically HTTPS/localhost. No WebXR session, positional tracking, SLAM, GPS registration or world anchors are implemented. Failed video.play() does not explicitly clean up an already acquired stream.

title: Optional device orientation
requirement: Allow orientation-based look; request permission where the browser exposes requestPermission, map alpha to yaw and beta to clamped pitch, and remove the listener on disable.
status: Static source evidence; device path untested
verification_or_acceptance: Inspect permission branch and orientation handler.
limitation: A success toggle does not prove the device emits usable sensor events or aligns with the model north direction.

title: Speech and screen-reader announcements
requirement: Send announcements to an aria-live region; optionally synthesize speech, canceling prior speech before each utterance. Offer full-route reading, per-segment navigation announcements during playback, scripted surroundings descriptions and a stop control.
verification_or_acceptance: Inspect announce(), full-route reading and surroundings-description handlers.
limitation: Descriptions are templates, not scene recognition. The surroundings template always says step-free/emerald guidance even in standard or high-contrast mode. Speech availability and intelligibility were not device-tested.

title: Directional audio beacon
requirement: When enabled, emit a 440–700 Hz sine ping approximately every 1.6 s while a route is active and before arrival; pan by the relative angle where StereoPanner is supported, otherwise output unpanned audio.
verification_or_acceptance: Inspect oscillator, pan, fallback and throttling expressions.
limitation: Playback of audio depends on browser/audio-device support and user activation. This is a heading cue, not acoustic localization or obstacle detection.

title: Caption demonstration
requirement: Cycle five fixed EN or five fixed ES PA-style strings every 5.2 seconds; permit language switching and optional pinning of the same string to a floating caption bar.
verification_or_acceptance: Inspect PA_CAPTIONS, setInterval and language/pin handlers.
limitation: No live event feed, microphone transcription or translation service is present. Language selection affects these captions, not the whole application.

title: Sensory-room shortcut
requirement: Select the sensory-room destination, enable low-sensory weighting, reset the route and close the drawer.
verification_or_acceptance: Inspect the shortcut handler assignments.
limitation: It does not set stepFreeOnly=true. If the user previously selected standard mode, the shortcut keeps standard mode despite its step-free toast.

title: High contrast and visual scaling
requirement: Toggle a high-contrast CSS palette and rebuild scene overlays; scale chevrons by exactly 1.6 when oversized arrows are selected, and set the root font scale to 1.18 in large-text mode.
verification_or_acceptance: Inspect CSS tokens, arrowScale and display toggle handlers.
limitation: The code does not calculate or audit 7:1 contrast, including over live video; fixed inline colors and canvas imagery also exist. WCAG AAA conformance is an intent claim, not an established implementation fact.

title: Reduced motion
requirement: Initialize from prefers-reduced-motion, offer a manual toggle, shorten CSS animations/transitions, stop decorative arrow/ribbon/ring/torch animation updates, and snap camera height/orientation instead of easing when applicable.
verification_or_acceptance: Inspect the media-query initialization, CSS override and animation guards.
limitation: The render loop, auto-walk and input-driven camera movement continue. This is reduced decorative motion, not a guarantee of no motion.

title: Navigation UI accessibility affordances
requirement: Provide a skip link, visible focus styling, labeled controls, pressed/selected/expanded states, drawer tabs and dialog roles; permit Escape to close the drawer and dialogs.
verification_or_acceptance: Inspect markup and attribute updates.
limitation: No modal focus trap, focus restoration, inert background or complete ARIA tab keyboard pattern is implemented. Accessible markup alone does not establish usability or conformance.

title: Escort request demonstration
requirement: Open an assistance dialog with five request categories, a route-segment-start waypoint, fixed coordinate text and active destination. Confirming reveals a fixed ticket/ambassador/three-minute message and announces it.
verification_or_acceptance: Trace dispatch handler: it only changes a CSS class and announces a string.
limitation: The assistance dropdown value is never read by dispatch. No ticket is created or transmitted; coordinates are not measured, no ambassador is contacted, and the displayed support contact is unverified.

title: Embedded specification and local export
requirement: Display the embedded requirements panel, offer re-running six built-in checks, and export a fixed Markdown specification via Blob and an object URL.
verification_or_acceptance: Inspect the check list, spec-modal handlers and Blob download code.
limitation: The exported text repeats authored claims; it does not derive a new specification or include the current verification evidence. Built-in tests do not establish real-world accessibility.

title: Initialization and responsive rendering
requirement: On window load, calculate the default route, run the built-in checks, and start requestAnimationFrame rendering. Resize renderer/camera with the window; adjust mini-map dimensions at the 640 px CSS breakpoint.
verification_or_acceptance: Inspect initialization order, resize handler and responsive styles.
limitation: The label “60FPS” is not enforced by a performance check or adaptive quality mechanism.

title: Integration and persistence boundary
requirement: Keep route settings, current pose and demo interactions in browser memory. This file contains no application API client, login flow, persistent settings storage, Azure service calls, GitHub calls or city-dataset loader.
verification_or_acceptance: Reviewed application network/storage/API references: only external static dependencies and device media APIs are present.
limitation: No connection to the previously collected curb-ramp/traffic datasets is implemented. CDN availability is required unless assets are separately bundled; reloading resets state.

title: Understand directions naturally
requirement: As a spectator, I want directions in my forward view so I can navigate without mentally rotating a stadium map.
verification_or_acceptance: Proposed user validation: observe representative users finding a destination using cues; measure wrong turns, assistance needed and reported confidence. Agree targets with users.
limitation: The existence of arrows does not establish comprehensibility.

title: Trust a route suited to mobility needs
requirement: As a wheelchair or mobility-device user, I want routes that respect my access needs so I can travel confidently and with dignity.
verification_or_acceptance: Proposed user validation: review verified end-to-end paths with mobility-device users, including crossings, widths, landings, entrances, lifts and closures.
limitation: Only the modeled stairs/slope exclusion is implemented. Trust and physical accessibility remain unvalidated.

title: Choose useful destinations
requirement: As a spectator, I want to find accessible seating, club access, companion-care facilities and a quiet room from a recognizable entrance.
verification_or_acceptance: Proposed user validation: confirm the destination vocabulary and facilities with attendees and venue staff, then test selection tasks.
limitation: The preset destinations are not a complete or independently verified venue directory.

title: Choose sensory and environmental comfort
requirement: As someone sensitive to noise or sun exposure, I want quieter or shadier options and a quick way to find a calm space.
verification_or_acceptance: Proposed user validation: compare perceived comfort and acceptable detours using verified shade/noise conditions and participant preferences.
limitation: Weights use fixed metadata, do not guarantee globally minimum noise or maximum shade, and are not live measurements.

title: Receive directions through usable channels
requirement: As a blind, low-vision, deaf or hard-of-hearing spectator, I want equivalent directions through visual, spoken and nonvisual cues so I can use the channels available to me.
verification_or_acceptance: Proposed user validation: test core navigation tasks with screen readers, speech/audio cues and text under representative venue conditions.
limitation: Caption content is simulated; audio output and screen-reader access have not been user-tested and do not prove equivalent access.

title: Adapt visibility and motion
requirement: As a user with visual or motion sensitivity needs, I want adjustable contrast, text, arrow size and motion so directions remain legible and comfortable.
verification_or_acceptance: Proposed user validation: test readability, contrast and motion comfort across device sizes, lighting and simulated/live-camera backgrounds.
limitation: No fixed contrast-compliance result or usability target is inferred from labels.

title: Preview and control the journey
requirement: As an attendee preparing for a visit, I want to preview a route at a suitable pace and viewpoint, pause it, inspect surroundings and revisit waypoints.
verification_or_acceptance: Proposed user validation: have users rehearse a trip, change viewpoint/speed and resume without losing orientation.
limitation: Playback demonstrates the virtual route, not actual travel time or physical positioning.

title: Keep guidance while using a camera
requirement: As an attendee, I want a familiar transition from preview to camera-based guidance, with a usable fallback when camera access is unavailable.
verification_or_acceptance: Proposed user validation: test permissions, fallback and switching on representative devices; separately verify real-world registration before navigation use.
limitation: Video overlay exists in source, but physical alignment and positioning are absent. A camera overlay is not a verified on-site AR navigator.

title: Keep the display understandable and calm
requirement: As a spectator, I want essential instructions to be prominent while optional details can be collapsed so I can see the path and avoid information overload.
verification_or_acceptance: Proposed user validation: measure task completion, missed hazards and perceived overload on small/large screens with and without panels open.
limitation: The stated >75% unobstructed viewport is not measured or enforced and is not adopted as a proven requirement.

title: Ask for appropriate human assistance
requirement: As a spectator needing help, I want to request the appropriate assistance with location context and receive a trustworthy status update.
verification_or_acceptance: Proposed user validation: validate dispatch workflows, acknowledgement, failure handling and location accuracy with venue accessibility staff and users.
limitation: The current confirmation is a UI demonstration, not a completed request or genuine ETA.
